verses.text: Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have obtained a like precious faith with us in the righteousness of our God and Savior, Jesus Christ:
Grace to you and peace be multiplied in the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord,
seeing that his divine power has granted to us all things that pertain to life and godliness, through the knowledge of him who called us by his own glory and virtue;

by which he has granted to us his precious and exceedingly great promises; that through these you may become partakers of the divine nature, having escaped from the corruption that is in the world by lust.
Yes, and for this very cause adding on your part all diligence, in your faith supply moral excellence; and in moral excellence, knowledge;
and in knowledge, self-control; and in self-control perseverance; and in perseverance godliness;
and in godliness brotherly affection; and in brotherly affection, love.
For if these things are yours and abound, they make you to be not idle nor unfruitful to the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
For he who lacks these things is blind, seeing only what is near, having forgotten the cleansing from his old sins.
Therefore, brothers,  be more diligent to make your calling and election sure. For if you do these things, you will never stumble.
For thus you will be richly supplied with the entrance into the eternal Kingdom of our Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ.
Therefore I will not be negligent to remind you of these things, though you know them, and are established in the present truth.
I think it right, as long as I am in this tent, to stir you up by reminding you;
knowing that the putting off of my tent comes swiftly, even as our Lord Jesus Christ made clear to me.
Yes, I will make every effort that you may always be able to remember these things even after my departure.
For we did not follow cunningly devised fables, when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we were eyewitnesses of his majesty.
For he received from God the Father honor and glory, when the voice came to him from the Majestic Glory, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”
We heard this voice come out of heaven when we were with him on the holy mountain.
We have the more sure word of prophecy; and you do well that you heed it, as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns, and the morning star arises in your hearts:
knowing this first, that no prophecy of Scripture is of private interpretation.
For no prophecy ever came by the will of man: but holy men of God spoke, being moved by the Holy Spirit.

footnotes.content: Peter names himself by his true name—Simon—before all his titles. How like Jesus, who still knows each of us by the real heart beneath our history. A servant of Jesus Christ is no small thing; it's the name given to all who've been broken and made whole by grace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Peace that multiplies—not by our earning, but by knowing Him more. I've watched grace work this way: the deeper we step into Jesus, the deeper the quiet settles in our bones.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Everything for godliness is already given. Not a scarcity we must scramble to achieve, but an inheritance waiting in His hands. We're poor only if we fail to recognize what He's already placed in our care.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To become sharers in divine nature—this is the great reversal. We fled from lust and its rot; now we're invited into His very life. The corruption we escaped was never our final word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Faith isn't idle; it works. Peter knows us—how we can believe truly yet sit still, forgetting that belief that lives is belief that grows. Supply means building, stone on stone, the house of your faith.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The ladder climbs: excellence births knowledge, knowledge produces restraint, restraint deepens patience, patience anchors us in godliness. No rung is skipped; each bears the weight of the next.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: And here love crowns it all—not abstract, but the kind we feel for family. Godliness left cold is counterfeit; it must warm into affection, then bloom into love, or the whole ladder was kindling.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Abundance in these things means we won't be idle or unfruitful. A soul growing in virtue bears fruit without striving; the fruit follows faithfulness like a shadow follows the sun.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Blindness creeps up quietly—you forget the cleansing. How easy to lose sight of what He washed away, to live as though we're still slaves to the old stain. Remembering mercy is seeing sight restored.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Make your calling and election sure. Not anxious certainty, but lived certainty—the kind you build by choosing steadily, day after day, not to stumble. The stumble comes not from one fall but from carelessness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: An entrance richly supplied into the eternal Kingdom—what a phrase. Not squeaking in by grace alone, but arriving laden with the freight of faithfulness, welcomed as family into His kingdom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Peter knows they know. Yet he writes on, because knowing and living are not the same, and a truth spoken again becomes a truth that grips deeper. Sometimes love means repeating the gospel we've heard.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He calls his body a tent—so temporary, so easily taken. It stirs him to write, to awaken, to make every word count. There's beauty in how mortality clarifies what matters most.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jesus made clear to Peter his end. Peter knew death was coming—not as fear, but as a road already mapped. There's peace in knowing the way you'll go, especially when the Hand that holds you is faithful.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even his death won't silence him. Peter pens his witness now so it speaks long after he departs—a grandparent's gift to generations he won't meet. Some words outlive the lips that spoke them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Peter says it plain: not fables, but eyewitness. He stood on the Mount of Transfiguration and saw Jesus' face shine. He's not theorizing—he's remembering. The Resurrection isn't doctrine to Peter; it's the man he touched.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Father's voice broke through heaven itself to honor the Son. Peter heard it. When the Father publicly delights in Jesus, what else could we need to know about who He is?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: We heard this voice—that little 'we' carries such weight. Peter doesn't stand alone testifying to strange inner feeling; he stands with others who heard the same thunder from heaven on a holy mountain.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Prophecy is a lamp in darkness, more sure than sight. We have it now—that sure word to guide us until the morning star dawns in our hearts. Hold to it in the dark hours; it never misleads.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No prophecy is a private matter. One soul can't simply decode Scripture according to whim; it speaks to the body, and the body interprets together. Beware the interpreter who claims special keys you lack.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in these words: the Spirit moved prophets then, and still moves His Word now. What was written under heaven's breath continues to breathe life into those who listen.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
